outcome: No resolution, partial resolution, or bound movement on Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs/L_{omega_1,omega} was found in the window; the general conjecture remains open, as it was on 26 January 2024.
summary: I could not confirm the triage's flagged lead and traced it to a search-engine hallucination. Multiple independent web searches repeatedly returned a claim that 'a new case of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in tame AECs' was established 'as of August 24, 2026,' always attached to the description of Vasey's paper 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in tame AECs with primes.' I fetched that paper's actual arXiv abstract page (arXiv:1509.04102) directly: it was submitted 14 September 2015, with six revisions running through 20 January 2017, and was published in Mathematical Logic Quarterly in 2018 — nearly a decade before the date being asserted. I also queried the arXiv API directly (an authoritative, non-summarized source) for every paper whose abstract contains the phrase 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture,' sorted by submission date descending: the most recent hit is Christian Espindola's 'A short proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AEC's with interpolation, under GCH' (arXiv:1909.13713, submitted 30 September 2019). Nothing from 2024, 2025, or 2026 exists in arXiv's own index under that phrase. The 'August 24, 2026' date therefore has no basis in any primary source I could locate; it is a fabrication produced by the search tool's summarization layer, most likely conflating the paper's content with the search's own execution date context. Broader searches for AEC/categoricity papers in the 2024-2026 window turned up several real, dated papers (Mazari-Armida/Vasey/Yang, June 2024; Hyttinen/Puljujarvi/Quadrellaro, May 2024; Beard, January 2026; papers on limit models arXiv:2503.11605 and arXiv:2511.18665), none of which prove a new case of, or move a bound on, the general Shelah eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs/L_{omega_1,omega} — they address adjacent structural questions (limit model isomorphism, stability, axiomatizability) without connecting back to the categoricity transfer statement. The one genuine categoricity-conjecture proof I found in this period, Saroch and Trlifaj's 'Deconstructible abstract elementary classes of modules and categoricity' (arXiv:2312.02623), proves a version of the conjecture for a specific class of module categories; its v1 was submitted 5 December 2023, which is before the 26 January 2024 frozen-revision date, so even setting scope questions aside this cannot count as an in-window event. Its v2 (30 September 2024) only added an appendix with an alternative, ZFC-model-dependent route to a weaker hypothesis on the same already-published theorem, not a new resolution. Wikipedia's own 'Abstract elementary class' article, which is where this bullet's context lives, still states 'as of 2014, the original conjecture remains open' with no update. No AI involvement was found or claimed anywhere in this research, consistent with the conjecture being untouched in the window.
competing_reading: If the Saroch-Trlifaj module-categoricity theorem is read as a genuine restriction (case) of the general L_{omega_1,omega} conjecture rather than a related/parallel statement in a different formal setting, it would still not change the status: it predates the frozen revision (v1: 5 December 2023) and so would be classified open_stale at most, not a change within the window. I lean toward treating it as a related result rather than a strict case because the authors explicitly frame deconstructible module classes as not automatically AECs, and their bound and hypotheses differ from the standard AEC categoricity-transfer framework — but this is a judgment call a specialist might make differently.
what_would_settle_it: A primary source — an arXiv listing, a named author's homepage, or an expert digestion (e.g. a post by Vasey, Baldwin, or on the Model Theory blog) — explicitly dated between 26 January 2024 and today that states a new case of, or bound on, Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs or L_{omega_1,omega} sentences. None was found despite direct arXiv API queries.
